name: Pixel Art
what_it_means: Pixel Art design brings back the blocky graphics of 8- and 16-bit games: bitmap fonts, chunky pixel icons, stepped edges and limited palettes. On modern clean layouts (like the reference post) it feels nostalgic, playful and handcrafted while staying readable.
signature_moves: Bitmap / pixel fonts for headlines and nav
Icons and illustrations built on a visible pixel grid
Limited palette, often on a clean light background
Retro game UI: health bars, score counters
best_for: Gaming, creative agencies, indie products, playful portfolios
prompt_template: B U I L D Y O U R U I R E P L A C E T H E [ B R A C K E T S ] ** Design an agency homepage for [STUDIO] in a Pixel Art style on a modern, clean layout. Light grey background (#F1F1F4). A giant headline in a blocky pixel font (Press Start 2P / PP NeueBit) in electric blue (#2A1FE0), with a black pixel subheading underneath. Navigation and labels in a monospaced bitmap font (VT323). Decorate with pixel-art icons drawn on a visible grid: a red 3D-ish pixel heart, pixel clouds, sparkles. Hot-pink (#FF4FB8) pixel button with a hard 1-step shadow. Stats row with big pixel numbers (20+, 85+, 42+). Use image-rendering: pixelated; no anti-aliased curves.
